$comment: Explicit reviews of the data that crates of the Rust kernel carry into the WebAssembly module (WASM-013; ADR 0016, decision 5). A crate that carries Unicode data (its licence names a Unicode licence, or it is one of the unicode-*, icu* crates) or hyphenation patterns (hypher, hyphenation, hyphenopoly) needs an entry for its exact version, with an expiry date; the licence gate (scripts/licence-gate.ts) fails without one. A hyphenation crate also lists the licence of every pattern file compiled in, and the option taken when a file offers a choice (docs/research/2026-11-06-borrow-list.md, section 11). An entry is a review, not an adoption: a crate the owner has not chosen (hypher) has no entry until it is. The owner chose unicode-linebreak and unicode-segmentation on 2026-11-18 (decision 224 of docs/owner-decisions-2026-11-15.md).

reviews.data: The ID_Start and ID_Continue property tables of the Unicode Character Database (UAX #31), as compact lookup tables. A dependency of wasm-bindgen-shared, listed by `cargo tree --edges normal,no-proc-macro` for wasm32-unknown-unknown, so it is in the module's dependency tree; whether the linker keeps its tables after link-time optimisation is not checked.
reviews.finding: The crate is `(MIT OR Apache-2.0) AND Unicode-3.0`: its code is under MIT or Apache-2.0 and the tables under the Unicode licence. The Unicode licence (version 3, 2023) is permissive: it asks that the copyright and permission notice appear in the documentation or notices that accompany copies of the data. Unicode-3.0 is on the allow-list of licences/policy.json. The crate's LICENSE-UNICODE file is part of the element's third-party notices (scripts/release/release.ts writes the notices of the crates compiled into the module) and of its bill of materials.
reviews.decision: WASM-013, lane w6, 2026-11-18 (proposed; a maintainer confirms)

reviews.data: The Line_Break property of every code point of Unicode 15.0.0 as a compact trie, and the pair table of the Line Breaking Algorithm (UAX #14), about 65 KB of source (src/tables.rs), generated from the Unicode Character Database. It is the module's line-break data for all scripts; the crate offers no way to leave a script out. The crate alone fails 59 of the 7,654 cases of the Unicode Consortium's LineBreakTest.txt of 15.0.0; the kernel corrects them (crates/layout-kernel/src/segment.rs) and passes every case. The corrections need two more tables of the same Unicode version, which are the project's own file and not the crate's: crates/layout-kernel/src/segment_data.rs (29 opening brackets of East Asian width and 35 ranges of unassigned Extended_Pictographic code points), generated by packages/layout-kernel/scripts/segment-data.ts from the Unicode Character Database 15.0.0 as the Perl of TeX Live ships it, the source of crates/layout-kernel/src/bidi_data.rs as well.
reviews.dataLicence: Unicode data of the Unicode Terms of Use (Unicode-3.0 for the data files), as the crate does not state it
reviews.finding: The crate's licence is Apache-2.0 (the LICENSE file is the Apache licence text and Cargo.toml says Apache-2.0), which is on the allow-list of licences/policy.json. The crate names no licence for the tables it generated from the Unicode Character Database, and ships no notice for them. The Unicode data files are published under the Unicode Terms of Use (the licence of Unicode 3.0 since 2023), which permit this use if the copyright and permission notice is kept with copies of the data. Open for a maintainer: whether the third-party notices of the release (scripts/release/release.ts) should carry the Unicode notice for these tables; this entry does not decide it. The last release is from 2023-07-25 and the crate implements Unicode 15.0.0 while the other segmentation crate implements 17.0.0. The two conformance test files that this story added (tests/data/SOURCES.json) are under the same terms; they are test data and are not compiled into the module.
reviews.decision: WASM-007, lane w6, 2026-11-18, on owner decision 224 (proposed; a maintainer confirms)

reviews.data: The Grapheme_Cluster_Break, Word_Break and Sentence_Break property tables of Unicode 17.0.0 (UAX #29), generated by the crate's scripts/unicode.py, about 293 KB of source (src/tables.rs). The kernel uses the grapheme tables only, and link-time optimisation removes the others: the first values of the crate's grapheme lookup table are in the built module, and those of its word and sentence lookup tables are not (looked for as bytes in the build of 2026-11-20; WASM-007 Evidence).
reviews.dataLicence: Unicode data of the Unicode Terms of Use (Unicode-3.0 for the data files), as the crate does not state it
reviews.finding: The crate is MIT OR Apache-2.0 (both licence files are shipped), which is on the allow-list of licences/policy.json. As with unicode-linebreak, the crate names no licence for the tables it generated from the Unicode Character Database and ships no notice for them; the Unicode Terms of Use ask that the copyright and permission notice is kept with copies of the data. Open for a maintainer: the notice in the release's third-party notices. The crate has no dependency (it can be built without the standard library) and no -sys crate.
reviews.decision: WASM-007, lane w6, 2026-11-18, on owner decision 224 (proposed; a maintainer confirms)

reviews.data: None: the crate has no data tables. It is in the dependency tree because HarfRust (the kernel's shaper, WASM-006) depends on read-fonts, which depends on yoke and zerofrom.
reviews.dataLicence: Unicode-3.0 (the crate's own licence; no data)
reviews.finding: The crate is yoke, a helper of part of the ICU4X project and its licence is Unicode-3.0 (MIT-style, with the Unicode notice). It is a zero-copy and ownership helper (a dependency of read-fonts and harfrust through the font parser) and carries no Unicode data tables: the licence is the project's, not a data licence. Unicode-3.0 is on the allow-list of licences/policy.json. Its LICENSE file is part of the element's third-party notices (scripts/release/release.ts) and of its bill of materials.
reviews.decision: WASM-006, lane w6, 2026-11-18 (proposed; a maintainer confirms)
